_comment: llmops-sfn-execution -- the state machine's own role. It existed live from Phase 3 but
was declared NOWHERE in this repo: created by hand, never reconciled by 01_iam.py, and
listed in PROJECT_STATE.md as if 01_iam.py owned it. Undeclared infrastructure is a
role nobody can review and nobody can rebuild -- a fresh-account deploy would have
produced a pipeline whose state machine could not start.
The DynamoDB grant is what lets the state machine close out its own runs. Until it
existed, a stage Lambda that CRASHED (as opposed to escalating politely) left the run
at status=running forever, because every Python writer of that field lives inside the
Lambda that just died. Nine live runs were zombies this way.
UpdateItem only, on the two tables that hold a lifecycle this execution ends.
The state machine is not allowed to create either record (start_pipeline mints
the run, the console mints the task) or delete them: its writes are terminal
statuses for work it is already executing.
llmops-tasks is here because the conductor's task row had the same zombie hole
the run record had, one level up: MarkTaskDone/MarkTaskFailed close it out. Those
states Catch States.ALL so that a run with no task (schedule, webhook) does not
fail, which means a MISSING grant here is indistinguishable from a healthy no-op
-- the execution succeeds and the task stays 'dispatched' silently. Hence the
test that reads every TableName out of the ASL and requires it in this policy.
